cells.tense: You're setting the shape of things right now, and your own hand is on it.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've been holding ready — put it into form today, while it's still small enough to shape.
cells.core:
Not a frame you inherited and not one that got handed to you — you laid this out yourself, and it's holding what you put in it. You can feel which piece belongs where, and so can the people standing in what you built. That's a hand that knows its own work.

A pattern like this invites the next thing. Set one more piece down and you'll learn what the structure can actually bear — where it flexes, where it resists, what it was always meant to hold. That's what this clarity is free to feed: one more piece of form, offered while it's still yours to shape.
cells.sheetLine: You're setting the shape, and the shape is holding.
cells.verb: beginning the first form of what will be built
cells.place: in the part of a life that sets the pattern and holds the structure

cells.tense: You're building ahead of the thing itself — setting structure for a form that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Let one structure you've drawn stay unfinished today, and find out what it actually holds.
cells.core:
The frame goes up around what's already there, loose enough that the shape can still surprise you. You put a container around something real and it grows into it. That's the working picture, and you've done it before.

Right now you're laying out the whole architecture before the first piece is in your hand. Every conversation gets its frame, every opening its rules, every unknown its plan — and the building is getting heavier than whatever it was meant to hold. Structure that arrives before the thing does stops being a container and starts being a cage. Put the blueprint down for one day and let the shape show itself from what's actually there. That's what Completion does — it waits for the whole to be whole before it names it.
cells.sheetLine: You're building the frame for something that hasn't shown up.
cells.verb: beginning the first form of what will be built
cells.place: in the part of a life that sets the pattern and holds the structure

cells.tense: You've stopped laying out the shape at all — the structure you knew how to make isn't coming out of your hands.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you already know is the right shape, and let that be enough to start.
cells.core:
You walk into the room and the pattern is already clear to you — the work arranges itself around what you can see, and other people lean on it. You know how it feels to set something down that holds.

Right now there's a form you could give this and you're not giving it. Someone else's structure governs the room, or the whole thing runs without one, and you've gone quiet about the pattern sitting right in front of you. What's missing isn't the ability to see it. It's the hand that sets it down. You know the shape. Say it plainly to one person today — not the finished plan, just the line of it. That comes from Clarity, and it's yours to give without asking permission first.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape and you're not saying it.
cells.verb: beginning the first form of what will be built
cells.place: in the part of a life that sets the pattern and holds the structure

cells.tense: You're already setting the pattern here — the shape of things is following your hand, and you're talking about it as though it grew on its own.
cells.ask: Claim one structure you've been calling just how things are — say that you set it, once.
cells.core:
You set a shape and you say so. You point at the thing you built and call it yours, and that naming is half of why it holds — people know where the pattern comes from, including you.

The shape in the work around you came from somewhere, and it came from you. How things are arranged, how the week runs, what counts as settled — you decided that. But you'd say it was just the way things ended up, nothing much to do with you. The author is in the room, arranging. The name isn't signed. One piece of the pattern that's really yours — say so, today. Definition is what that is: the plain beginning of something you've been building without saying you were.
cells.sheetLine: You set the pattern. You're calling it just how things are.
